source.commit_body:
The previous suppression window incorrectly neutralized volume signal on
{D-1, D, D+1} for any earnings event on date D, ignoring the existing
EarningsDate.call_time field. This nuked volume signal on the trading
day BEFORE earnings (a clean session) and missed AMC events whose impact
falls on the next trading session across weekends/holidays.

Correct semantics, now implemented in compute_earnings_suppressed_dates():
  BMO   (call_time < 09:30 ET): suppress earnings_date itself
  AMC   (call_time >= 16:00 ET): suppress next trading day after earnings
  INTRADAY (09:30-16:00 ET, rare): suppress earnings_date itself
  UNKNOWN (null/unparseable): conservative {ed, next_trading_day}

Trading-day awareness via PriceHistory dates handles AMC-Friday ->
Monday correctly, plus weekend/holiday earnings -> first trading day.

Smoke test on AAPL 2024-2025 (8 quarterly AMC earnings on Thursdays):
  OLD: 24 dates suppressed (Wed+Thu+Fri per event)
  NEW:  8 dates suppressed (Friday only per event)

Old code was zeroing volume signal on ~16 clean trading days per stock
per year (the day before + day of earnings). Universe-wide, this was
suppressing meaningful volume events on tens of thousands of trading
days where there was no actual earnings interference.

Files:
  volume_amplifier.py
    - _classify_call_time(str) -> BMO/AMC/INTRADAY/UNKNOWN
    - compute_earnings_suppressed_dates(rows, trading_dates) -> Set[date]
    - _analyze (DB path): inline call_time-aware check using PriceHistory
      for prev trading day + gap-day detection
    - _analyze_from_cache: parameter renamed earnings_suppressed_set,
      single-set membership lookup replaces 3-day window scan

  database/models/core.py (2 callers, calculate_scores_batched +
  recalculate batched path):
    - Load (date, call_time) tuples
    - Pass through compute_earnings_suppressed_dates with PriceHistory
      dates as trading calendar

  simulator.py:
    - StockContext now takes earnings_rows (date, call_time) tuples
    - Bulk load extended to fetch call_time
    - earnings_set built via compute_earnings_suppressed_dates

  test_volume_amplifier.py:
    - 17 new unit tests cover BMO/AMC/INTRADAY/UNKNOWN classification,
      Friday-AMC -> Monday carryover, weekend earnings, conservative
      UNKNOWN handling, the D-1-must-not-be-suppressed regression, etc.

This is a scoring change — volume_signal/volume_magnitude flow into
Score.overall via the volume amplifier multiplier. Requires
trader recalculate --force --full to rescore historical data with
the corrected suppression set.
